subject: Re: Optera renewal - request to accelerate 'freshness' SLA feature
messages:

Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Optera renewal — request to accelerate 'freshness' SLA feature

Team,

Quick summary: Optera (Sarah Lowe, procurement) has made our renewal conditional on an explicit SLA for model-output freshness and worst-case tail latency when a model is updated. They want an operational guarantee that requests served after a model update will observe the new weights within X minutes and that cold-starts won’t exceed a 120ms P99 for their primary workload.

Attached is their requirements doc (requirements_optera_v1.pdf) and a draft SOW. The ask: can we commit to an MVP of a "freshness SLO" mechanism (combination of targeted cache warming + routing preference) that we can demo by March 1? Optera is one of the largest renewals this quarter ($1.2M ARR).

Asks for this thread:
- Jasmine / Product: is there a path to deliver an MVP (config + controls) in ~2 weeks or do we need deeper runtime work?
- Dev / Eng: estimate on effort and any gating risks.
- Kim / CS: what interim mitigations can we offer if we can't deliver full feature by March 1?

I know this is tight; Sarah is explicit that this is decision-driving. Please reply with availability for a 30m sync today.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Forwarding the request from Marissa — Optera is pushing for a March 1 commit. I added Dev and Jasmine.

Some context from my side: Optera is running models with frequent nightly weight updates (regulatory retraining). Their compliance team needs deterministic exposure to the newest model within the maintenance window. They are also sensitive to tail latency because of live clinical workflows.

Marissa — if there are any hard non-negotiables in the SOW draft, flag them inline.

Michael

Subject: Re: Optera renewal — request to accelerate 'freshness' SLA feature

Thanks for the context. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we scope: 
1) Do they require an absolute guarantee (platform-managed switch-over) or is a contractual SLO with documented mitigation acceptable?
2) Which models/workflows are in scope (full traffic vs a subset)?
3) Is the freshness window defined (e.g., new weights visible within 5 minutes of deployment)?

High level: if we can satisfy with config-level controls (priority routing + pre-warm hooks + explicit model-version pinning for the Optera tenant) we can likely ship a productized control surface faster. If the requirement is runtime-level (kernel-level state sync to ensure 100% determinism across nodes), that’s heavier and needs an eng spike.

I can move this into the roadmap as an "enterprise SLA accelerator" candidate, but need concrete scope to decide whether to deprioritize other work.

Available for a 30m sync at 10:45 or 11:30PT today.

-jasmine

--
Jasmine Liu
Group PM, Platform | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, michael_grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-02-14T13:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Optera renewal — request to accelerate 'freshness' SLA feature

Quick technical readout from infra/runtime:
- Short answer: an MVP that meets their ask via existing knobs (explicit per-tenant model-version pinning + orchestration-led prewarming) is feasible in ~2–3 weeks if we accept manual playbooks and on-call support. That avoids deep runtime changes.
- Full automation (platform-level guarantee that new weights are visible within N minutes across all nodes without manual steps) requires kernel/runtime work: coordinating KV cache invalidation + deterministic KV sync. Estimate: 4–6 weeks for an eng spike + an additional 3–4 weeks for stabilization and perf testing.
- Risk: high concurrency tenants and multi-AZ fallbacks increase the edge-case surface; we may need a short canary of traffic to validate P99 claims.

Interim mitigations:
1) Pre-warm job triggered at model deploy for Optera tenant (scoped, no infra changes).
2) Temporary routing rule to route Optera traffic to a reserved pool (dedicated warm pool) during the first 24 hours post-deploy. This requires capacity reservation but is doable.

I attached a short technical proposal describing the prewarm + routing approach (eng_proposal_optera_v1.pdf). If Sales can commit to the reserved pool cost (or accept an ARR credit), we can turn the interim mitigation into a reliable short-term SLA.

- Dev

--
Dev Patel
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Optera renewal — request to accelerate 'freshness' SLA feature

Thanks Dev — this is helpful. A few additional deal facts to influence prioritization: 
- Deal size: $1.2M ARR (renewal + expansion).
- Optera procurement is explicit: if we can't show an operational plan (MVP or reliable interim with reserved pool) by March 1 they will pause the contract renewal and open the RFP to other vendors.
- They are sensitive to credits — giving a big ARR credit to hit the date will likely kill the unit economics we promised to Finance.

Proposed tradeoffs:
- Option A (preferred by Optera): Eng delivers a working MVP (prewarm + routing control surface) in 2 weeks and we roll with an SLA pilot for 90 days.
- Option B (fallback): We offer a reserved warm pool for Optera for 3 months at a dedicated pool surcharge (passes cost to customer) and we deliver the automation behind the scenes in 6–10 weeks.

If Product and Eng can commit to Option A timeline (2 weeks for an MVP with manual operational steps documented), I will push hard on Optera to accept the pilot approach rather than demanding an immediate platform-level SLA.

Marissa
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

I can own the operational rollout for Optera if Eng can deliver the prewarm + routing hooks as an MVP in ~3 weeks and provide a clear playbook. CS will run the pilot with Optera's compliance team and collect telemetry for the P99 claims.

If we agree to the reserved warm pool option, CS will need clarity on billing (surcharge vs credit) and an escalation path for any SLA misses during the pilot.

Proposal: 30m sync tomorrow 10:00PT to lock scope and sign off on who owns the playbook and monitoring.

-Kim
